teams.synopsis: The top team for the second straight week — the last undefeated squad in the league.
teams.blurb: The top team for the second straight week, Max's squad has proved yet again why he's the favorite in 2024. The last undefeated team in the league — now the question isn't whether he'll lose, but rather will he lose. Going undefeated is a tall task, but with his stars having staggered bye weeks until Week 12, it's still possible. There's not much to question with this team, and I fully expect another dominant performance in Week 5.

teams.synopsis: The third time at the 2-spot in four weeks — a 3-1 record and the 2nd-most points scored in the league.
teams.blurb: The third time at the 2nd spot in the past four weeks, Tony Fkn Romo is here to stay. A 3-1 record combined with the 2nd-most points scored in the league is enough to label Aidan as an elite team contending for its first PFFL championship. Despite having <mark class="hl-player">Goedert</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">St. Brown</mark> on bye this week, the team is still primed for a top-5 week.

teams.synopsis: A locked-in top-3 team for a 5th straight week — injuries to Hollywood and Rice may open the door for Worthy.
teams.blurb: Not a fall from grace yet, Routensss is a locked-in top-three team for now, with this week marking the 5th straight week of being ranked in the top 3. It should be noted that the injuries to <mark class="hl-player">Hollywood</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Rice</mark> may have opened the door for <mark class="hl-player">Worthy</mark> to become an every-week flex play at the very least. Nonetheless, a bad performance this week against Gorman may be enough to drop out of the elite group.

teams.synopsis: At the 4-spot for the third straight week — never below 112, never above 128 in any given week.
teams.blurb: For the third week in a row, Brandon finds himself at the number-4 spot. Brandon has yet to produce less than 112 points in any given week, but on the other end he has also yet to produce more than 128 points in any given week. With <mark class="hl-player">Montgomery</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Dobbins</mark> on bye this week, it'll be very interesting to see how <mark class="hl-player">Mattison</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">White</mark> hold up as the team's RB1 and RB2.

teams.synopsis: The hot take turned out to be true, for now — Nico Collins is on pace for 2,000 receiving yards.
teams.blurb: The hot take turned out to be true... for now. Deniz's team showed out in Week 4, bringing the team its first win of the season. Led by <mark class="hl-player">Nico Collins</mark>, who may finish as the WR1 this season and is on pace for over 2,000 receiving yards, the team is looking to get back to .500 in the coming weeks, which starts with a matchup against Carmine in Week 5.

teams.synopsis: Cracking the top 6 for the first time all season, continuing to win despite the injuries.
teams.blurb: Cracking the top 6 for the first time all season, Ethan's team continues to win despite the injuries. This three-game win streak may be coming to an end in Week 5 against a sneaky Geg team, but being in this position with the given situation is pretty surprising. I expect this team to continue floating around this playoff-bubble area of the rankings, at least until the injuries go away.

teams.synopsis: The highest ranking of the year — jumping four spots on the strength of Daniels, Kyren, and Taylor.
teams.blurb: The highest ranking of the year comes for Charlie in Week 5, with a jump of 4 spots from 11 to 7. Led by a big three of <mark class="hl-player">Daniels</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Kyren</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Taylor</mark>, this team looks primed for a win streak as the wide receivers begin to produce and the bench depth fills out. On the downside, Taylor looks to be sidelined for at least 1-2 weeks with an ankle injury, but <mark class="hl-player">Bucky Irving</mark> will be a fine replacement in the meantime.

teams.synopsis: The epitome of rollercoaster emotions — 111, 120, 72, 136 through four weeks, still chasing playoff consistency.
teams.blurb: Just as I said last week, this team is the epitome of rollercoaster emotions. His point totals for the first 4 weeks are 111, 120, 72, 136. He's now trying to solidify himself as a playoff team, and another great performance in Week 5 will do just that. Quin has a ton of trade assets on his team, but without trades this team can still be a challenge to beat.

teams.synopsis: Another sub-100 week keeps Rolls out of the top 8 — but no real bye trouble until Week 11.
teams.blurb: Another sub-100 performance in Week 4 has Rolls staying out of the top 8. The 2-2 team looks to separate himself from the bottom-five teams in the coming weeks, and with no real bye trouble until Week 11, the time to stack wins is now. Perhaps it's been a stroke of good luck that his team has escaped injuries, or maybe it's just grit. Whatever it is will help the team get back into the playoff picture in the weeks to follow.

teams.synopsis: The biggest dropper this week after losing Rashee Rice to a knee injury — a tough matchup looms.
teams.blurb: The biggest dropper of the week, Potty lost his WR1 in <mark class="hl-player">Rashee Rice</mark> to an undisclosed knee injury. This week will be a challenge for Ryan, as he goes against a top-3 opponent, but a plethora of good matchups for his players may just unlock a hidden ceiling we haven't seen just yet. Overall, the drop to 10 may be an overreaction to the injuries, but it'll be interesting to see how the seasoned manager moves through these next few weeks.

teams.synopsis: Out of the top 10 for the first time all season — a brutal bye week opens the door to test the depth.
teams.blurb: Out of the top 10 for the first time all season, Grits looks to bounce back in Week 5 against a top opponent. A brutal week of byes for Baylen's team, with <mark class="hl-player">Gibbs</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">McConkey</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Jameson Williams</mark> all being off. However, this opens the door to see what his depth can really do, with players like <mark class="hl-player">Tre Tucker</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Josh Downs</mark> now in the starting lineup.

teams.synopsis: Dropping from 8 to 12 — the talent for a top-8 team is there, but the players just aren't producing together.
teams.blurb: Dropping from 8 to 12, GOC has the talent to be a top-8 team, but the players just aren't producing simultaneously. The poor play up to this point from <mark class="hl-player">Mahomes</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Stevenson</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Pittman</mark> is really limiting this team's weekly upside. It wouldn't shock me if the team booms this week, but then again, unless trades are made, GOC won't have the production to contend.

teams.synopsis: Out of 14th for the first time since Week 2 — not because Ben improved, but because Carmine got worse.
teams.blurb: Moving back out of the 14th spot for the first time since Week 2, but not because the team had a good week — rather, Carmine's had a worse one. Another team with an 0-4 start, Ben looks to get his first win of the year against a short-handed Minutemen. On the bright side, <mark class="hl-player">Hockenson</mark> may be returning soon and <mark class="hl-player">Addison</mark> may be a solid flex, but only time will tell.

teams.synopsis: Not much to say — an 0-4 start hits like a train, and the WR trio underwhelmed more than the RBs.
teams.blurb: Not much to say, an 0-4 start hits like a train. The running back positions were viewed as the downfall of this team, and yes they performed just as we expected, but it was the underwhelming wide receiver trio of <mark class="hl-player">Wilson</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Olave</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Smith</mark> that may have led to this brutal beginning. It's tough to see the defending champ be a month into his 2024 campaign without a win, but there's still plenty of time.
